data.body:
Possibly relevant field evidence from an AWS CloudTrail audit (2026-07-30), offered as data rather than a diagnosis.

Among today's `bedrock:Converse` calls, four failed within a single second with a model-identifier error distinct from the parameter-deprecation errors that bug 1903 covers:

    2026-07-30T20:34:23Z  ValidationException: The provided model identifier is invalid.   (x4)
    2026-07-30T16:03:39Z  ValidationException: Invocation of model ID anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
                          with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request with the
                          ID or ARN of an inference profile.

Why this may bear on this ticket: if `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` is parsed and documented but read by nothing, then whatever id actually reaches `Converse` comes from another source, and these are the observable symptoms of the id that is really being sent. The 16:03:39Z line in particular shows a bare foundation-model id being used where an inference-profile id is required.

I have NOT traced these calls to a specific code path and cannot confirm they originate from the unread config key — they were made under `user/joe_frontier` during interactive Bedrock work, so they may equally be manual experimentation. Treat as a lead to confirm or dismiss, not as evidence of the defect.

Cross-ref: 1903 (temperature/top_p override table), 9249 (instance-role Bedrock access).
